disposition_reason: Tables 1 and 2 give arsenic, cadmium, lead and mercury by ICP-MS on fresh weight in pooled spinach, carrot, potato and apple and in four fish (canned tuna, anchovy, sea trout, farm trout) bought in Istanbul.

study.origin: potatoes, spinach and apples garden grown, carrots greenhouse grown (regions not stated); fish (except canned tuna) from the Marmara Sea
study.market: local markets in Kartal, Maltepe and Sariyer (produce) and Bakirkoy, Pendik and Uskudar (fish), Istanbul, Turkey
study.method: ICP-MS (Agilent 7700) after microwave digestion of 0.5 g wet sample in HNO3/H2O2
study.lod_text: not reported separately; less-than values printed for arsenic and mercury
study.qa: calibration standards and internal standards listed; no CRM or recovery reported

findings.group: pooled from local markets in Kartal, Maltepe and Sariyer, Istanbul
findings.integrity_flag: Table 1 arsenic values for carrot, potato, spinach and apple are identical to the values the Discussion (p. 70) attributes to Shaheen et al. 2016; the arsenic row may be reprinted or mis-cited, so its provenance is unresolved
findings.notes: Printed as a less-than value (censored upper bound); one pooled composite sample.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Per-portion loads compared with JECFA and Turkish Food Codex portion limits (fruits and vegetables)
regulatory_or_exposure.value: e.g. lead 33.6 (carrot), 53.5 (spinach), 29.7 (potato), 40 (apple) ug per portion vs 7.8, 37.35, 7.29, 9.2 ug

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Turkish Food Codex limits used for fish
regulatory_or_exposure.value: As 1, Cd 0.05 (anchovy 0.30), Pb 0.2 (tuna) or 0.3, Hg 0.5 mg/kg

unresolved: Arsenic values in Table 1 match exactly the values the Discussion cites from Shaheen et al. 2016 (potato <0.0007, carrot <0.00073, spinach 0.01234, apple <0.00074 ug/g); whether the arsenic row is the study's own data cannot be confirmed.
Abstract says lead was highest in spinach; Table 1 has apple 0.436 above spinach 0.430 ug/g.
Table 3 prints apple mercury per portion as 0.031 without the less-than sign carried by the other three; the text gives <0.031.
Table 4 heading says ug per portion but prints the same values as the Table 2 concentrations.
Per-portion loads (Tables 3 and 4) are derived and not recorded as findings.
Each food is a single pooled composite, so no dispersion is available.
